hints: Model both particles with upward positive and acceleration $-g$; at collision they have the same height above the ground at the same time.
For P, $y_P=30t-\frac12gt^2$. For Q, which starts $15\,\mathrm m$ higher, $y_Q=15+10t-\frac12gt^2$.
Set $y_P=y_Q$; the identical gravity terms cancel, leaving a linear equation for the collision time.
Substitute that time into either height expression and verify the particle has not yet reached the ground.
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Formulate the equations of vertical motion under gravity ($g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$) taking upward displacement from the ground as positive:
For particle $P$ ($u = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$, initial height $0\text{ m}$):
$$y_P(t) = 30t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = 30t - 5t^2$$
For particle $Q$ ($u = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$, initial height $15\text{ m}$):
$$y_Q(t) = 15 + 10t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = 15 + 10t - 5t^2$$

Step 2: Set $y_P(t) = y_Q(t)$ to find the time of collision:
$$30t - 5t^2 = 15 + 10t - 5t^2$$
$$30t - 10t = 15$$
$$20t = 15 \implies t = \frac{15}{20} = 0.75\text{ s}$$

Step 3: Substitute $t = 0.75\text{ s}$ into either position function to calculate the collision height:
$$y = 30(0.75) - 5(0.75^2) = 22.5 - 5(0.5625) = 22.5 - 2.8125 = 19.6875\text{ m}$$
The particles collide at a height of $19.7\text{ m}$ (exact: $19.6875\text{ m}$) above the ground.

hints: Treat the collision and the subsequent fall as separate stages, using collision time $0.75\,\mathrm s$ and height $19.6875\,\mathrm m$ from part (a).
Immediately before impact, use $v=u-gt$ to find the upward velocities of P and Q from their initial speeds $30$ and $10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.
Conserve upward signed momentum as the particles combine: $0.1v_P+0.4v_Q=(0.1+0.4)V$.
The combined particle initially moves upward with speed $V$, then eventually falls to ground through a net vertical displacement of $-19.6875\,\mathrm m$.
Use $v^2=V^2+2g(19.6875)$ for the impact speed at the ground and take the positive magnitude.
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Calculate the vertical velocities of $P$ and $Q$ immediately prior to impact using $v = u - gt$ ($t = 0.75\text{ s}$):
$$v_P = 30 - 10(0.75) = 30 - 7.5 = 22.5\text{ m s}^{-1}\text{ (upwards)}$$
$$v_Q = 10 - 10(0.75) = 10 - 7.5 = 2.5\text{ m s}^{-1}\text{ (upwards)}$$

Step 2: Apply the conservation of linear momentum to the coalescing particles ($m_P = 0.1\text{ kg}$, $m_Q = 0.4\text{ kg}$):
$$m_P v_P + m_Q v_Q = (m_P + m_Q)V$$
$$(0.1)(22.5) + (0.4)(2.5) = (0.1 + 0.4)V$$
$$2.25 + 1.0 = 0.5V$$
$$3.25 = 0.5V \implies V = \frac{3.25}{0.5} = 6.5\text{ m s}^{-1}\text{ (upwards)}$$

Step 3: Apply the work-energy theorem or kinematics formula $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ for the combined body falling to the ground from $h = 19.6875\text{ m}$:
Taking downward motion as positive (or using energy conservation):
$$v^2 = V^2 + 2gh$$
$$v^2 = (6.5)^2 + 2(10)(19.6875) = 42.25 + 393.75 = 436.0$$
$$v = \sqrt{436.0} \approx 20.8806\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 20.9\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The speed of the combined particle on reaching the ground is $20.9\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
